biological.citation: Semaphorin heterodimerization in cis regulates membrane targeting and neocortical wiring (PMID: 39152101)
biological.summary: In murine neocortex, Satb2 controls neuronal migration and callosal axon outgrowth by inducing expression of the GPI-anchored Sema7A. Sema7A heterodimerizes in cis with Sema4D and promotes Sema4D plasma membrane targeting. This places Satb2 upstream of a Sema7A/Sema4D semaphorin pathway relevant to SATB2-associated syndrome.

biological.citation: SATB2 preserves colon stem cell identity and mediates ileum-colon conversion via enhancer remodeling (PMID: 34582804)
biological.summary: SATB2 is a colon-restricted chromatin factor that preserves LGR5+ colonic stem cell identity in mice and humans. Satb2 loss converts colonic stem cells into ileal-like stem cells, and SATB2 modulates enhancer binding of CDX2 and HNF4A. Human colonic organoids acquire ileal characteristics when SATB2 is lost.

biological.citation: Protein translation rate determines neocortical neuron fate (PMID: 38849354)
biological.summary: A small-molecule screen identified Ire1α as a regulator of Satb2 expression and neuronal polarity. Satb2 mRNA translation requires eIF4A1 helicase activity acting on its 5'-UTR. Satb2 expression in cortical neurons is therefore controlled post-transcriptionally by translation.

biological.citation: Satb2 is required for the regionalization of retrosplenial cortex (PMID: 31666685)
biological.summary: In Satb2 conditional knockout mice, the Rsp/subiculum boundary is lost, Rsp-specific genes are lost, and subiculum genes are ectopically expressed. Satb2 acts as a transcriptional repressor of Nr4a2 and Ctip2, and this repression specifies retrosplenial identity cell-autonomously.

biological.citation: The expression profile and function of Satb2 in zebrafish embryonic development (PMID: 20814748)
biological.summary: Zebrafish satb2 is ubiquitously expressed from the 1-cell to the 10-somite stage, then becomes restricted to the pronephric duct (24 hpf), branchial arches (36 hpf), and retinal ganglion cell layer and fins (48 hpf). Knockdown arrests embryos at 50-60% epiboly, impairs cell migration, and reduces dynamin II and VAMP4. Knockdown also disorganizes actin and the yolk syncytial layer.

biological.citation: SATB2 drives glioblastoma growth by recruiting CBP to promote FOXM1 expression in glioma stem cells (PMID: 33124191)
biological.summary: SATB2 is preferentially expressed in glioma stem cells. It binds the MAR of the FOXM1 locus and recruits the histone acetyltransferase CBP to activate FOXM1 and drive proliferation. SATB2 knockdown reduces GSC proliferation and GBM growth, and the CBP inhibitor C646 suppresses growth in vitro and in vivo.

biological.citation: Satb1 and Satb2 regulate embryonic stem cell differentiation and Nanog expression (PMID: 19933152)
biological.summary: Satb2 is upregulated in Satb1-/- ES cells. Forced Satb2 expression in wild-type ES cells antagonizes differentiation-associated silencing of Nanog, and both Satb1 and Satb2 bind the Nanog locus in vivo. Satb1 and Satb2 thus act antagonistically on Nanog expression and pluripotency.

biological.citation: SATB2 expression increased anchorage-independent growth and cell migration in human bronchial epithelial cells (PMID: 26780400)
biological.summary: Ectopic SATB2 expression in BEAS-2B cells increased anchorage-independent growth and migration. shRNA knockdown reduced growth in Ni-transformed cells. RNA-seq showed SATB2-regulated genes enriched in cytoskeleton, cell adhesion and cell movement pathways. SATB2 expression is also induced in cells transformed by As, Cr, Ni and V.

biological.citation: miR-29a-5p Targets SATB2 and Regulates the SIRT1/Smad3 Deacetylation Pathway to Inhibit Thoracic Ligamentum Flavum Cell Osteogenesis (PMID: 32205703)
biological.summary: SATB2 is upregulated in ossified thoracic ligamentum flavum tissue, and miR-29a-5p directly targets and suppresses it (dual luciferase assay). SATB2 knockdown reduced SIRT1 expression and Smad3 acetylation and blunted the miR-29a-5p effect on osteogenesis, placing SATB2 upstream of the SIRT1/Smad3 pathway.

biological.citation: Multiomic profiling of transcription factor binding and function in human brain (PMID: 38831039); ASHG 2023 - Extensive profiling of transcription factors in postmortem brains
biological.summary: ChIP-seq in human postmortem brain shows that the neuronal TFs SATB2 and TBR1 bind unique regions depleted of high-occupancy sites. These regions regulate and promote neuron-specific gene expression, consistent with SATB2 acting as a neuronal transcriptional regulator.
